sessions.phase_label: Revised selection process and extended trial
Requalification clips and iterative quality review
Production onboarding and Instagram account setup
First live clip batch, corrections, approval, and publishing
Clip-variation workflow update and engagement closure

requirements.title: Initial Three-Clip Trial
requirements.definition: The initial task-local assignment to produce three short-form trial clips for evaluation against the client's brand and editing standards.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the first completed and reviewed trial assignment; later extended and renewed trials are separate assignments with independent quantities and acceptance outcomes.

requirements.title: Extended Trial Clip Batch
requirements.definition: The later task-local trial assignment to produce a larger batch of brand-compliant clips after the selection process was revised.
requirements.boundary_note: This 15-to-20-clip trial is distinct from both the completed initial trial and the subsequent July requalification assignment.

requirements.title: Requalification Clip Batch
requirements.definition: The renewed qualification assignment requiring revised clips to demonstrate conformity with the detailed examples and quality standards before production work.
requirements.boundary_note: The changes from three retry clips to focused revisions and then one reference-matching clip are stages of one renewed qualification trajectory, not changes to the recurring production quota.

requirements.title: First Live Clip Batch
requirements.definition: The task-local assignment to prepare the first production clips intended for client approval and live publication.
requirements.boundary_note: This first live batch has its own quantity, correction, approval, and publication trajectory and is separate from qualification trials and the recurring monthly quota.

requirements.title: Monthly Approved Clip Quota
requirements.definition: The recurring production obligation measured by the number of client-approved clips completed each month.
requirements.boundary_note: The monthly quantity and recurrence belong here; detailed approval rules, compensation, deadlines, and individual trial batches are separate concerns.

requirements.title: Clip Source Selection
requirements.definition: Rules governing selection of source material from Teyron's long-form YouTube content for conversion into short-form clips.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement covers allowable source material and source-video choice; hook quality and whether the selected moment forms a complete lesson are independently testable Requirements.

requirements.title: Clip Hook Quality
requirements.definition: Each clip should begin with a strong, effective hook capable of attracting and retaining viewer attention.
requirements.boundary_note: Hook selection can be trained, revised, and varied independently of the clip body, duration, caption styling, and lesson completeness.

requirements.title: Complete Teaching Moment
requirements.definition: Each clip must present a self-contained lesson, story, or meaningful point from beginning to end so that it provides value and is understandable on its own.
requirements.boundary_note: Lesson completeness and standalone comprehension form one tightly coupled content criterion; duration is separate because a clip can meet the duration rule while still ending mid-lesson.

requirements.title: Short-Form Channel Targeting
requirements.definition: Produced clips should be suitable as standalone short-form content for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.
requirements.boundary_note: This captures the intended output channels; actual Instagram account setup, post metadata, cadence, and publication authorization are separate operational Requirements.

requirements.title: Clip Duration
requirements.definition: Clips must remain within the client-confirmed duration range or minimum duration used for approval.
requirements.boundary_note: Duration has its own changing numeric acceptance criteria and can fail independently of lesson completeness or editing quality.

requirements.title: Caption Presentation
requirements.definition: Rules governing the clip captions' color, font, effects, outline or shadow, placement, and visual stability.
requirements.boundary_note: Caption typography and placement are attributes of one presentation mechanism; general transitions and visual effects outside the captions belong to clean visual editing.

requirements.title: Clean Visual Editing
requirements.definition: Clips must use polished, simple editing without distracting animations, heavy effects, or flashy transitions.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers general edit effects and transition style, excluding caption-specific formatting, B-roll placement, and audio behavior.

requirements.title: Natural B-Roll Integration
requirements.definition: B-roll should be incorporated where it naturally strengthens the spoken message rather than being inserted randomly or merely as filler.
requirements.boundary_note: B-roll selection and placement can be modified and reviewed independently of the underlying lesson, captions, effects, and audio mix.

requirements.title: Background Music Mix
requirements.definition: Clips should use mood-appropriate background music at a low level that never overpowers Teyron's voice.
requirements.boundary_note: Music choice and voice-relative volume are independently testable from environmental-noise cleanup.

requirements.title: Audio Noise Cleanup
requirements.definition: Undesired recording noise, including wind noise, should be removed when preparing clips.
requirements.boundary_note: Noise removal has its own concrete failure and fix trajectory and therefore remains separate from background-music mixing.

requirements.title: Clip Approval Gate
requirements.definition: A clip counts toward production and may proceed to publication only after client review and approval, with rejected clips requiring correction.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the acceptance workflow; the monthly quota owns only the recurring quantity, while individual content and technical standards own the reasons a clip passes or fails.

requirements.title: Clip Submission Package
requirements.definition: Clips submitted for review must be delivered through the specified shared package, including the requested folder naming and link-access configuration.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers the review-delivery artifact and access configuration, not project deadlines or the later logging of published Reel links in Notion.

requirements.title: Clip Variation Reuse
requirements.definition: A clip body may be reused to create additional approved variations by replacing the hook or opening, subject to the permitted reuse count.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently actionable production method rather than merely an attribute of hook quality or the monthly quota.

requirements.title: Dedicated Instagram Account
requirements.definition: A dedicated Instagram content account must be configured with official-looking branding, a Teyron image or logo, and profile text and links that route viewers to the main account.
requirements.boundary_note: Profile identity, branding, bio, and main-account routing form one configured account artifact; credential values and secret-transfer details are explicitly excluded.

requirements.title: Approved Clip Publishing
requirements.definition: Approved clips must be published as Reels on the assigned Instagram content account and the resulting post link reported when requested.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers the publication action and destination; approval rules, caption metadata, posting cadence, and Notion logging can each change independently.

requirements.title: Instagram Post Metadata
requirements.definition: Each published Reel must include the prescribed follow caption, hashtag set, and in-post tag for the designated main account.
requirements.boundary_note: Caption, hashtags, and account tagging are tightly coupled post-metadata attributes; uncertainty about the correct handle should be handled in the Event lifecycle rather than by splitting the Requirement.

requirements.title: Instagram Posting Schedule
requirements.definition: Approved clips must be spaced and published according to the specified cadence and peak-hour posting window.
requirements.boundary_note: Posting time and one-per-day spacing are independently actionable operational constraints, separate from post metadata and the clip's technical content.

requirements.title: Post Activity Logging
requirements.definition: After each Reel is published, its posting date and Instagram link must be recorded on the corresponding Notion card.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a distinct operational recordkeeping behavior that remains required after the publication action itself succeeds.
